purpose: UI/UX storyboard; example data; layout approved, implementation pending
sharedStyle:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create one high-fidelity desktop web-app screenshot concept, landscape 16:10, edge-to-edge app UI, no device frame, no decorative presentation border, no montage. Product name BizBox. This is a UI/UX mockup with invented example data, not a real operating product. Tiny visible badge "Design preview · Example data".
DESIGN SYSTEM IDENTICAL ACROSS ALL STAGES: sleek restrained dark liquid glass. Graphite/navy translucent panels, subtle smoky blur, hairline pale borders, readable near-white modern sans-serif typography, muted silver secondary text, small icy periwinkle-blue accent, no green. No excessive blobs, ornamental orbs or neon. Clean strong hierarchy, dense enough to be useful but generous breathing room. Simple 12px radius, subtle refraction at panel edges. Crisp legible UI text, short copy only. Refined production product feel, not sci-fi dashboard.
LAYOUT IDENTICAL: minimal top bar 60px high with BizBox wordmark left, "Bean There / Los Angeles" center-left, small project menu right. Main region below: 68% width interactive 3D geographic map or cutaway interior on LEFT, 32% width persistent dark translucent consultant dock on RIGHT. Shared slim bottom strip in left viewport for current selection or playback when relevant. Map fills its area, real-looking spatial Los Angeles street grid, detailed believable 3D building blocks in bird's-eye oblique view, roads and intersections, warm evening lighting and subdued materials. It MUST look three-dimensional and spatial, never a flat map or city skyline photo. Map is visual concept geometry, do not suggest site-verified geometry. Selected space uses a periwinkle outline and small pin. No photo used as a substitute for map.
Right dock: header "Consultant", clearly visible segmented "Text | Voice" control, compact thread, user and assistant distinguishable without huge bubbles, input pinned to bottom reading "Ask about this location…" with attachment and send icon. Keep conversation contextual to left viewport. Only stage-relevant controls, no giant KPI walls, no redundant paragraphs or navigation rail.
Use consistent fictional example "Space A · Los Angeles", coffee shop "Bean There", rent "$4,500/mo". Baseline 2 service stations, 3 staff, $6 average order. Only metrics explicitly specified by stage. Any customer movement is modeled, not measured pedestrian traffic. Interior must read as "Modeled layout" rather than verified scan. Source labels subtle but legible. No photo credits, slogans, question numbers, onboarding questions, implementation jargon or fabricated real property addresses.

stages.title: 1 · Arriving after onboarding
stages.prompt: CHECKPOINT 1: First arrival in main workspace after completed onboarding. LEFT: stable 3D bird's-eye Los Angeles neighborhood with three understated numbered pins A, B, C. Map controls small top left "Neighborhood" and map zoom/reset top right. Bottom left a concise floating horizontal shortlist containing 3 space mini-cards, A selected, clear rent and small modeled label; no charts yet. RIGHT consultant introductory one sentence "I found three spaces that fit your brief." A short recommendation card "Start with Space A" and two very short evidence bullets "Within your rent target" and "Compare morning demand". Three small actionable chips "Explore spaces", "Compare locations", "Test operations". Visible Text selected; composer. Main focus is onboarding context already carried forward, easy first next step. No modal covering map.

stages.title: 2 · Selecting a space
stages.prompt: CHECKPOINT 2: User selected Space A. LEFT still full 3D Los Angeles map, camera closer to a selected commercial block, target building outlined blue. A well-organized compact floating detail sheet over left bottom quarter: "Space A", "Los Angeles", rent "$4,500/mo", "Size not verified", a small plausible storefront thumbnail with "Example exterior", buttons "View interior" primary and "Compare" secondary. Keep most map visible. RIGHT user message "Tell me about Space A." Consultant short response "It fits your rent target. Let’s test how your service setup handles the morning peak." Under it compact linked evidence card with two rows "Rent · Example listing", "Demand · Modeled". Two quick actions "Open interior" and "Run baseline". No overconfident location recommendation or promised success.

stages.title: 3 · Understanding the interior
stages.prompt: CHECKPOINT 3: Enter interior before running. LEFT visual area switches from geographic map to stable beautifully rendered bird's-eye orthographic-ish cutaway coffee-shop floor plan, clearly "Interior · Modeled layout" at top left with back arrow "Neighborhood". Warm dark floor, coherent walls/entrance, counter, two labeled service stations "Station 1" and "Station 2", clear thin queue lane near entrance, modest tables. Accurate readable spatial interface, not a photoreal empty interior viewpoint. A couple of small neutral customer markers may show as static examples. Compact selected settings strip "2 stations · 3 staff · $6/order". Bottom playback control visibly PAUSED, timeline at 08:00, inactive state "Run baseline to begin". RIGHT consultant "This layout shows where queues and service happen." Short selectable labels "Entrance", "Queue", "Service stations" correspond to highlighted zones. Primary action "Run baseline". Text/Voice stays visible and thread continuous. No unsupported scans, no animated puddles or furniture editing controls.

stages.title: 4 · Setting up an experiment
stages.prompt: CHECKPOINT 4: Following baseline, user asks "What if I add a service station?" LEFT same modeled cutaway interior with baseline's two stations solid, proposed third station highlighted in fine blue dashed outline, readable labels. LEFT bottom a compact flat experiment tray titled "Alternative" with tactile polished sliders, strong tick spacing and clear current values: "Service stations  2 → 3" active slider, "Staff  3" unchanged, "Average order  $6" unchanged. Only 3 controls no huge form. Primary luminous restrained blue "Run alternative"; secondary "Cancel". Small "Baseline preserved". RIGHT consultant card "Test one extra station" with one sentence "Keep demand, staff and price the same." Clear concise diff "Stations 2 → 3". Below small neutral note "Station cost not included". Human explicitly runs; no Keep button yet and no simulation results invented before run. Composer and Text/Voice present.

stages.title: 5 · Watching the simulation
stages.prompt: CHECKPOINT 5: Alternative simulation playback, visible exactly what customer flow means. LEFT same clear bird's-eye modeled coffee interior now with three labeled service stations, small modeled customer dots traveling along tidy sparse trajectories, 2 or 3 dots queued near counter, selected dot with compact tooltip "Customer 12 · Waiting · 2 min". Not a decorative particle cloud. Bottom common playback bar with Play/Pause, speed "1×", seekable timeline "08:00 — 09:00", current time "08:32", "Alternative" selected; controls visually satisfyingly precise. Above bar compact three metric pills with EXPLICIT current-time context "At 08:32": "Served 18", "Waiting 3", "Left 1". Top left view segmented "Neighborhood | Interior" with Interior selected; top small status "Modeled arrivals". RIGHT consultant short contextual response "The queue is building at the counter." Two chips "Highlight queue", "Inspect customer". Small activity line "Playing alternative". Do not show full-hour future results while current time08:32. No chat scroll hijack, no giant charts, no flashy glowing footsteps.

stages.title: 6 · Comparing baseline and alternative
stages.prompt: CHECKPOINT 6: Finished run, compare options. LEFT same interior at completed 09:00 with clear segmented toggle "Baseline | Alternative" near top and Alternative selected. A compact readable comparison panel attached to lower part of left viewport, not obscuring entire scene: heading "Morning peak · 08:00–09:00", columns "Baseline" and "Alternative"; rows "Served 32 | 36", "Avg wait 7 min | 4 min", "Left 6 | 2". Under table tiny truthful note "Same modeled demand and seed". Bottom clock at09:00 paused. RIGHT consultant "The third station shortened waits in this example." Structured short diff card "2 → 3 service stations", outcome highlights "4 more served" and "3 min less waiting", neutral note "Added station cost not included". Two clear actions "Keep alternative" primary and "Revert" secondary. Link-like "View assumptions". No automatic claim this is profitable; no red-green finance dashboard. Explain one decision, preserve thread and selected site.

stages.title: 7 · Keeping the decision
stages.prompt: CHECKPOINT 7: User kept alternative. LEFT returns to same 3D Los Angeles map view with Space A selected, interior remains one click away via concise selection strip. A slim status pill "Alternative saved" in soft icy blue, not green. Bottom selected-site strip "Space A · Current plan" with short facts "3 stations · 3 staff · $6/order" and actions "Open interior", "View comparison". RIGHT conversation user "Keep the alternative." assistant "Saved as your current plan for Space A." One small tidy version card "Current plan · Alternative 1", details "3 service stations", link "Compare with baseline". Three next-step chips "Try another location", "Adjust opening hours", "Review assumptions". No celebratory confetti, no promises, no heavy report dashboard. Context remains continuous and saved decision visually unambiguous.

stages.title: 8 · Switching to Voice
stages.prompt: VOICE MODE COMPANION VIEW, same main workspace and same saved Space A context. LEFT actual geographic-looking 3D bird's-eye Los Angeles map with selected commercial building periwinkle outline and small "Space A · Current plan" bottom strip. RIGHT Consultant header with segmented Text | Voice, VOICE selected. Keep full map visible, no fullscreen voice takeover. In dock upper-mid area a restrained compact blue waveform (not giant orb) and status "Listening…", live transcript below "Could we compare this with the second space?", small contextual card "Space A · Alternative 1" showing same saved context. A collapsible section "Conversation" with two short previous turns visible under it. Bottom voice controls: clear microphone button, mute, "End voice", plus small "Type instead" link; no second chat thread. Dark translucent glass, high legibility, elegant minimal motion implied. Tiny label "Voice interaction concept" so mockup isn't claimed live.
